parsed.summary: The Lean theorem states the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality |⟪x, y⟫| ≤ ‖x‖‖y‖ for any two vectors x, y in a real inner product space F. Here F is a NormedAddCommGroup with InnerProductSpace ℝ F, and the norm is the one induced by the inner product. This matches the paper exactly. No caveats of substance: there are no bespoke definitions and no junk-value issues.

lean_claims.plain: For every real inner product space F (a normed additive group with a compatible ℝ-inner product) and all x, y ∈ F: |⟨x, y⟩| ≤ ‖x‖·‖y‖.

paper_claims.plain: For vectors x, y in a real inner product space, |⟨x, y⟩| ≤ ‖x‖‖y‖.

coverage.why: Same hypotheses (real inner product space) and same conclusion. The Mathlib InnerProductSpace class forces ‖x‖² = re⟨x, x⟩, so the norm is the induced one.
